messages.content: Find out about traffic laws in Texas.

function.name: lawsuit_search
function.description: Search for lawsuits related to a particular subject matter in a certain location. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The location to perform the search in.

subject.description: The subject matter of the lawsuits.

year.description: Optional. The year in which the lawsuit was filed. Default: 2024

message.content:
**Traffic Laws in Texas – Overview** | Topic | Key Points | |-------|------------| | **Speed Limits** | • Posted limits vary by road type (e.g., 55 mph on rural interstates, 45 mph on urban interstates).
• Speed limits may be reduced during construction or adverse weather. | | **Seat Belt Use** | • All occupants must wear seat belts.
• Children under 8 must use a child safety seat. | | **Driving Under Influence (DUI)** | • Blood Alcohol Concentration (BAC) limit is 0.08% for drivers over 21.
• Zero tolerance for drivers under 21 (any detectable BAC). | | **Cell Phone Use** | • Handheld phone use while driving is prohibited unless using a hands‑free system. | | **Right‑of‑Way Rules** | • At uncontrolled intersections, vehicles approaching from the right have priority.
• Pedestrians always have priority at crosswalks. | | **School Bus Regulations** | • Vehicles must stop when a school bus has its stop sign extended and lights flashing. | | **Lane Discipline** | • Drivers should stay within their lane unless turning or merging. | | **Headlights & Visibility** | • Headlights must be used from sunset to sunrise and during inclement weather. | | **Toll Roads** | • Texas has several toll roads; electronic toll collection (TxTag) is required for some. | | **Parking Restrictions** | • No parking in front of fire hydrants, driveways, or within 25 feet of a crosswalk. | For detailed statutes, consult the Texas Transportation Code or the Texas Department of Motor Vehicles website.
message.reasoning: The user wants information about traffic laws in Texas. They didn't specify a location or subject for lawsuit search. But they might want general traffic laws. We can provide an overview. There's no request for a lawsuit search. So we don't need to call the function. Just give them info.
